# dlartgp

> Generate a plane rotation with non-negative diagonal.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlartgp from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlartgp';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlartgp( f, g, cs, sn, r ) → void
```

Generates a plane rotation with non-negative diagonal.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `f` | `number` | First component of the vector to be rotated |
| `g` | `number` | Second component of the vector to be rotated |
| `cs` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the cosine of the rotation |
| `sn` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the sine of the rotation |
| `r` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the nonzero component of the rotated vector |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `f`: The first component of vector to be rotated.
- `g`: The second component of vector to be rotated.
- `cs`: The cosine of the rotation.
- `sn`: The sine of the rotation.
- `r`: The nonzero component of the rotated vector.

  This version has a few statements commented out for thread safety (machine parameters are computed on each entry). 10 feb 03, SJH.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlartgp.strided( f, g, cs, sn, r ) → void
```

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlartgp()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLARTGP`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlartgp.f).
-   This is a more accurate (and slower) alternative to the Level-1 BLAS routine `drotg`. Unlike `dlartg`, `dlartgp` always returns a non-negative `r`.
-   If `g = 0`, then `cs = sign(1, f)` and `sn = 0`.
-   If `f = 0` and `g != 0`, then `cs = 0` and `sn = sign(1, g)`.
-   The algorithm incorporates iterative rescaling to avoid overflow or underflow for inputs with extreme magnitude.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlartgp from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlartgp';

const cs = new Float64Array( 1 );
const sn = new Float64Array( 1 );
const r = new Float64Array( 1 );

dlartgp( 3.0, 4.0, cs, sn, r );
let result = new Float64Array( [ cs[ 0 ], sn[ 0 ], r[ 0 ] ] );
console.log( result ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

dlartgp( -3.0, -4.0, cs, sn, r );
result = new Float64Array( [ cs[ 0 ], sn[ 0 ], r[ 0 ] ] );
console.log( result ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLARTGP`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLARTGP generates a plane rotation so that

$$
\begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CS} & \mathrm{SN} \\ -\mathrm{SN} & \mathrm{CS} \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} F \\ G \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} R \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \quad\text{where}\quad \mathrm{CS}^2 + \mathrm{SN}^2 = 1
$$

This is a slower, more accurate version of the Level 1 BLAS routine DROTG, with the following other differences:

-   F and G are unchanged on return.
-   If $G=0$, then `CS`=(+/-)1 and `SN=0`.
-   If $F=0$ and (G .ne. 0), then `CS=0` and `SN`=(+/-)1.

The sign is chosen so that $R \ge 0$.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
